mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry in the Investor's Home Jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the home jurisdiction is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention (e.g., Hong Kong, Singapore, UK), obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority. If not a party (e.g., United Arab Emirates), follow consular legalization: notarize the certificate, authenticate it at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the home country, then legalize at the Chinese Embassy/Consulate.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or Certificate of Incumbency)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home Jurisdiction Companies Registry or Registered Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille if the issuing jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member; otherwise, consular legalization as described above. The certificate must be issued within 30 days prior to submission.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney appointing the local WFOE legal representative and signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the resolution, then obtain an Apostille (if applicable) or consular legalization. The document must be in Chinese or accompanied by a certified Chinese translation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or Memorandum and Articles) of the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign Investor's Corporate Secretary or Legal Counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization as per the home jurisdiction's status. The document must be certified as a true copy by a notary public.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Foreign Investor's Principal Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Bank where the Foreign Investor maintains an account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The letter must be notarized, then apostilled or consular legalized. It should confirm the investor's financial standing and that the account has been active for at least 12 months.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and senior managers against the following lists: (1) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (2) the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List; (3) the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (4) the Chinese Ministry of Public Security's List of Persons Subject to Anti-Money Laundering Measures; and (5) the World Bank Listing of Debarred Firms. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a real-time basis via automated systems, and at least annually. Enhanced due diligence is required for any match, including name and date-of-birth verification, and a risk-based assessment must be documented. For PEPs, a senior management approval is required before establishing a business relationship, and ongoing monitoring of the source of funds is mandatory. All screening results must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) and the local SAMR online name clearance portal (e.g., Shanghai or Beijing SAMR)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Chinese characters. The name must follow a four-tier structure: (1) administrative division (e.g., 'Shanghai'), (2) distinctive name (may be a transliteration of the foreign investor's name), (3) industry or business characteristics (e.g., 'Information Technology'), and (4) company type (e.g., 'Co., Ltd.'). For WFOEs, the distinctive name may include a phonetic transliteration of the foreign investor's name, but must not contain any Latin letters, Arabic numerals, or symbols unless approved by SAMR. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names in the same industry. The transliteration must comply with the Chinese Phonetic Alphabet (Pinyin) rules.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration with the local SAMR within 60 days of receiving the rejection notice. The appeal must include the original application form, the rejection notice, a written explanation of why the name should be approved, and any supporting evidence (e.g., trademark registration). The SAMR must issue a decision within 30 days. If the reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court within 90 days of the reconsideration decision. The court will review the legality of the SAMR's decision. It is advisable to consult with a Chinese legal counsel to prepare the appeal and ensure compliance with the Enterprise Name Registration Regulations (SAMR Order No. 1, 2021).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are generally not permitted for WFOEs in China. The registered office must be a physical address that is capable of receiving official correspondence and is accessible for inspection by the SAMR, tax authorities, and other regulators. For a software company engaged in remote desktop access and IoT telemetry, a virtual office would likely be rejected by the local tax bureau for the purpose of issuing VAT invoices and by banks for opening a corporate bank account. A physical lease agreement for at least one year is required, and the address must be consistent with the business license. Some free trade zones (e.g., Shanghai FTZ) may allow shared office spaces, but they must be registered as a legal business address and provide a lease certificate.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspections: (1) Verify that the registered address is physically occupied and has a visible company sign; (2) Ensure that the lease agreement is in the company's name and not subleased without permission; (3) Maintain a reception area and basic office equipment; (4) Have a designated person (e.g., the legal representative or a staff member) present during business hours. Risk assessment: For a newly incorporated WFOE in the software industry, the likelihood of an unannounced inspection within the first 12 months is approximately 30%. The local SAMR and tax bureau may conduct joint inspections to verify commercial substance, especially if the company applies for tax benefits or high-value invoices. The risk increases if the company uses a shared office or a residential address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: The Company Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), as currently in force; Articles 1, 2, 4, 98, 99, 100, 101, 102, 106, 108, 110, 111, 113, 128, 129, 154, 156, 162, 163, 172, 174, 175, 202, 206, 208, 387 and 397; the Foreign Investment Act, Articles 5, 6, 7 and 8; the Regulations on Foreign Investment Approval; and the Guidelines for Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Review.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (R.O.C.); foreign investment pre-approval is granted by the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Limited Company Incorporation Registration Application under Article 387 of the Company Act, filed together with the Foreign Investment Approval Letter, the capital verification report, the articles of incorporation, and the pro-forma first board resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Taiwan limited company. For a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE), the paid-in capital must equal or exceed the amount approved in the MOEAIC Foreign Investment Approval; the full amount must be remitted into a Taiwan bank account in the company's name before registration and verified by a Taiwan licensed CPA. There is no general blocked escrow account requirement, but the capital must remain traceable and un-disbursed until the company has obtained its registration certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY] LIMITED (WFOE). At a meeting of the first board of directors of [Company] Limited, duly convened and validly held on [Date], at [Time], at [Registered Office Address], Taiwan, upon due notice to all directors, the following resolutions were proposed, seconded, and passed unanimously. 1. ARTICLES AND BUSINESS PURPOSE: RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation of the Company, including the Statement of Business Purpose covering remote desktop access, unattended machine telemetry, screen sharing software, IoT connectivity, software publishing, and related consulting services, be and are hereby adopted and approved; and the Chairperson is directed to file the same with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and all other competent authorities. 2. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED, that the authorized and paid-in share capital of the Company be and is hereby established as [Capital Amount in TWD or USD], divided into [Number] shares of [Par Value] each; the sole shareholder [Foreign Investor] hereby subscribes to all such shares for cash, and the Board hereby accepts the subscription; the full amount of the subscribed capital shall be paid into the Company's designated bank account in Taiwan before the registration application is submitted, and a licensed CPA's capital verification report shall be obtained and filed. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [Registered Office Address], Taipei, Taiwan, and the Company Secretary is authorized to notify the Ministry of Economic Affairs of any change, lease, relocation, or amendment and to maintain the registered address in full compliance with applicable law. 4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the Company open corporate bank accounts, deposit accounts, foreign currency accounts, and online banking mandates with [Bank] at its Taiwan branch; the signatories, [Names and Titles], are authorized to open, operate, close, and manage all such accounts, execute bank mandates, approve payments, and access online banking; any two of the authorized signatories shall jointly sign checks, remittance instructions, and any payment instruction exceeding [Threshold Amount]. 5. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed Chairman and General Manager, [Name] be and is hereby appointed Chief Financial Officer, [Name] be and is hereby appointed Company Secretary, and [Name] be and is hereby appointed Compliance Officer, each with the duties, powers, and responsibilities set out in the Articles of Incorporation and the Company Act. 6. FILING AND EXECUTION AUTHORITY: RESOLVED, that the Chairman and Company Secretary are jointly and severally authorized to execute, sign, certify, seal, deliver, and file all applications, declarations, consents, powers of attorney, registration forms, tax documents, banking forms, and any other instruments necessary to complete the incorporation of the Company, the foreign investment approval, the tax registration, the labor and health insurance registration, and the opening of the Company's bank accounts. The Company Secretary is directed to record these resolutions in the minutes and to provide certified copies to the board. Certified by the Company Secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-registration Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company and Commerce Registration Information Center, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (R.O.C.) - online name review portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an electronic application for company name and business scope pre-review through the MOEA Company and Commerce Registration Information Center website. The proposed English name must be stated as the WFOE's statutory English name and must not conflict with an existing registered or reserved name, or contain prohibited terms relating to banking, insurance, or national security. The business scope must identify software publishing and remote screen-sharing IoT services. Once the name is approved, the reservation is valid for four months, during which the foreign investment approval and company registration application must be completed. Attach the foreign investor's certificate of existence and a signed letter confirming no objection to the proposed name.
required_dossiers: Company name pre-review application form
Business scope description in English
Certificate of incorporation of foreign investor, notarized and apostilled
Power of attorney appointing a Taiwan local agent
Written confirmation of the proposed English company name from the sole shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or challenged, file a written objection with the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days, or amend the proposed name and resubmit online immediately. If similarity with an existing registrant is cited, provide consent from the existing registrant or select a distinctive secondary name and reapply without loss of priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC), Taiwan - Foreign Investment Application Center / online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Foreign Investment Application together with the foreign investor's certificate of incorporation, board resolution authorizing the Taiwan investment, proposed articles of incorporation, capital remittance schedule, business plan, and audited financial statements or equivalent evidence of the investor's legal existence. The application must be filed before any inward capital remittance or company registration. MOEAIC will review the proposed investment against nationality restrictions, national security, and public policy. If approved, the MOEAIC approval letter will state the maximum approved amount of foreign capital and any conditions. All foreign corporate signatures must be notarized in the investor's jurisdiction and authenticated by a Taiwan overseas mission or apostille.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application form in English or Chinese
Certificate of incorporation of the foreign investor
Board resolution or shareholders' resolution of the foreign investor approving the Taiwan investment
Power of attorney in favor of the Taiwan filing agent
Proposed Articles of Incorporation in Chinese
Business plan including ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 classification
Capital remittance schedule
Audited financial statements or bank reference letter of the foreign investor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEAIC issues a request for supplementary documents, cure the deficiency within the statutory 14-day period by submitting the requested information. If approval is denied, the investor may file an administrative appeal to the Executive Yuan within 30 days of receipt of the denial, or restructure the investment vehicle and file a new application with corrected facts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inward Capital Remittance and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated Foreign Exchange Bank in Taiwan and a Taiwan licensed Certified Public Accountant (CPA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital deposit account in Taiwan in the name of the proposed WFOE using the MOEAIC approval letter, the company name reservation certificate, and the foreign investor's corporate documents. The foreign investor must remit the full approved paid-in capital from abroad to this account, and the bank must issue an inward remittance advice or certificate. The WFOE must then engage an independent Taiwan CPA to verify the remitted funds, confirm the capital is not loan proceeds, certify the paid-in capital amount, and issue a capital verification report. The capital must not be used, loaned, or withdrawn before the company registration application is filed and approved.
required_dossiers: MOEAIC Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Company name reservation certificate
Bank inward remittance advice or foreign currency deposit certificate
Temporary bank account opening application
CPA capital verification report
Articles of incorporation
Confirmation of source of funds from the foreign investor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank blocks the remittance due to anti-money-laundering or foreign-exchange control queries, provide the bank with the MOEAIC approval letter and source-of-funds documentation. If the CPA refuses to issue a clean capital verification report, correct any irregularity in the funding path and obtain a supplemental verification before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Incorporation Registration with the Department of Commerce, MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan - Company and Commerce Registration Information Center / online registration system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the incorporation registration application with the Department of Commerce through the official company registration system. The application must include the approved name certificate, the final Chinese articles of incorporation, the pro-forma first board resolution, the CPA capital verification report, the bank capital deposit certificate, the registered office lease and landlord consent, the directors' consent forms, the statutory officers' identification, and the MOEAIC foreign investment approval letter. The filing must occur within the validity period of the name reservation and within sixty days after completion of capital verification. The Department of Commerce will examine the legality of the incorporation; upon approval, the WFOE will receive the limited company registration certificate and a company registration identification number.
required_dossiers: Incorporation registration application form
Company name reservation certificate
Articles of incorporation signed by all shareholders
Pro-forma first board resolution
CPA capital verification report
Bank capital deposit certificate
Registered office lease or title document with landlord consent
Passport or ID copies of directors, shareholders, and statutory officers
Foreign investor board resolution and MOEAIC approval letter
Application fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Department of Commerce issues a deficiency notice, cure the application within the prescribed 15-day response period by submitting the missing documents or amending the articles. If registration is rejected, file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days or amend the defective documents and re-file a revised incorporation application without penalty except for applicable re-registration fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Labor, and Bank Activation Registrations After Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan); Labor Insurance Administration, Ministry of Labor; and the designated bank branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the company registration certificate is issued, register the WFOE with the appropriate local National Taxation Administration office within 15 days to obtain the unified business tax number and to register for business tax, withholding tax, and income tax. The WFOE must also register as an employer with the Labor Insurance Administration and the National Health Insurance Administration for any employees. Finally, present the company registration certificate, articles of incorporation, tax registration certificate, and capital verification report to the designated bank to convert the temporary capital account into an operating company account and activate corporate debit and credit facilities. All statutory filings must be completed before invoicing or payroll is processed.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate issued by the Department of Commerce
Articles of incorporation
Tax registration application form
Certified copy of the unified business tax number application
Labor insurance employer registration form
National health insurance employer registration form
Registered office lease or utility bill
Passport or ID of the Taiwan statutory representative
Bank operating account activation application
CPA capital verification report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed beyond the statutory period, file the late registration immediately and pay any assessed default interest; upon receipt of a tax penalty, apply for a leniency reduction under Article 49 of the Tax Collection Act or administrative reconsideration within 30 days. For denied bank account conversion, provide the additional bank-requested ownership or source-of-funds documentation and resubmit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations are established under ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210, which cover pure software publishing, remote desktop access, and telemetry software services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - the WFOE is a digital software and remote support services company and does not require an industrial or manufacturing operating license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - the Ministry of Environment (Taiwan) has no EIA jurisdiction over software-only business activities; no EIA filing or environmental permit is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable / Exempt from Full EIA and Environmental Registration because the WFOE will not operate factories, chemical plants, assembly lines, or warehouses within the ISIC categories requiring mandatory EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the company will not discharge wastewater, emit VOCs, generate hazardous industrial waste, or handle regulated toxic chemicals from its software operations; only ordinary office waste collection applies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no industrial civil defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or installation-grade occupational safety approval is required for a remote screen-sharing IoT software business. The registered office must, however, comply with standard Taiwan workplace safety requirements under the Occupational Safety and Health Act and local fire-prevention rules applicable to ordinary office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), acting through the local tax service authorities at the WFOE's registered address, and administered digitally through the State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau platform and the State Administration for Market Regulation one-stop enterprise registration system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The WFOE first obtains an 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) from the State Administration for Market Regulation; the USCC automatically constitutes the taxpayer identification number (TIN) and VAT registration number. Within 30 days after issuance of the business license, the legal representative or authorized agent must complete tax registration through the Electronic Tax Bureau portal, confirming the taxpayer type (resident enterprise), registered address, legal representative, ISIC 6201 software and information technology services industrial classification, capital structure, and bank account details. The Electronic Tax Bureau issues a digital tax registration certificate; the same USCC is used for all VAT filing and invoice issuance. A foreign non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment in mainland China may separately obtain a non-resident TIN through the Electronic Tax Bureau platform or through its PRC withholding agent by submitting its certificate of incorporation and tax residence certificate. For the Taiwanese shareholder/counterparty, such non-resident TIN is used for PRC withholding tax reporting; the Taiwan-invested WFOE itself remains a PRC resident enterprise

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China operates a dual current/capital account convertibility regime. The RMB is convertible on current account items such as trade in software services, remote support subscriptions, and bona fide cross-border service fees, provided the transaction is based on genuine commercial contracts and supported by invoices, contracts, and tax certificates. However, capital account transactions remain tightly restricted; FDI equity injections, shareholder loans, dividend distributions, and capital outflows require SAFE registration or approval, a clear commercial purpose, and use of designated foreign exchange accounts. For this mainland WFOE, all export revenue from remote desktop access and IoT telemetry services must be repatriated to China, reported under service trade foreign-exchange declarations, and cannot be netted or retained offshore without SAFE permission. Profit remittance is permitted only after annual tax filing, audit completion, and CPA confirmation of distributable profit, with corporate income tax and withholding tax settled. Foreign exchange transactions are subject to the actual-demand verification principle, and any anticipated hedging must be tied to real underlying exposure. In practice, this means current account convertibility is nominally available but documentary-intensive, while capital account mobility remains tightly controlled and liquidity-constrained.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The mandatory fixed-percentage surrender rule has been abolished. Export proceeds must be repatriated into mainland China through a licensed collecting bank and registered in the SAFE trade-monitoring system within the applicable timeline. For goods exports, the standard collection period is generally within 90 days from the date of customs declaration, while service exports such as software and IoT telemetry are expected to be settled and repatriated promptly once due. The WFOE may elect to retain 0% or up to 100% of foreign currency earnings in its foreign exchange settlement account, or convert them into RMB, subject to bank verification of the underlying export contract, customs manifest where applicable, invoice, and collection entry. The conversion ratio is not a statutory fixed rate but must match the stated commercial purpose and the actual-demand principle.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Exchange Capital Account) for FDI equity injection; RMB Basic Deposit Account for operational treasury

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account and RMB Basic Operational Currency Account
FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account and RMB Basic Operational Currency Account
FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account and RMB Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable as a primary treasury rail. A mainland-incorporated WFOE must use a licensed Chinese bank with SAFE visibility for all onshore FX and cross-border settlement. Offshore digital EMIs, including UK or European e-money institutions, cannot open a local RMB account for the WFOE and are not designated FX banks. Using Stripe or Paddle as a merchant of record for global software and IoT subscription sales is acceptable for customer-facing collection, but settlement into China must be routed through an onshore acquiring or settlement arrangement with proper service trade foreign-exchange declarations. EMIs cannot act as flow-through vehicles for FDI capital injection, capital account remittance, or outbound trade disbursements, and any attempt to use an EMI as a treasury intermediary would violate the PRC foreign exchange control framework.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: First-time account opening for a mainland WFOE generally requires the legal representative or a senior authorized officer to appear physically in the bank branch to execute account forms and complete a face-to-face KYC interview. Remote-only consular proxy opening is not permitted for a newly formed WFOE. After the principal KYC has been completed, a remote finance manager or appointed signatory can be added via a notarized power of attorney and video interview. For a Taiwan-resident shareholder, corporate and identity documents must be notarized in Taiwan and processed through the legitimate cross-strait notarization exchange channels before the mainland bank will accept them. The statutory director must also be prepared to explain the business model, source of funds, expected transaction patterns, and the technical nature of remote screen-sharing and IoT telemetry software.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-strait shareholder jurisdiction elevates PEP and source-of-funds review because the Taiwan investor is treated as a foreign investor; opaque personal shareholding trusts or intermediate offshore holding companies may trigger beneficial ownership scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certified certificates of incorporation and records of directors of the Taiwan holding entity; signed declaration of ultimate beneficial owner and the full controlling chain; six months of bank statements from the remitting shareholder account with documented savings, dividends, or legitimate operating income; and audited financial statements for each intermediary holding layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FDI capital account injection with purpose mismatch; funds arriving through personal accounts or without SAFE registration; mixing current account software subscription revenue with capital account equity funding may trigger reclassification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate for FDI, capital injection contract, board resolution for equity subscription, bank remittance advice with the exact FDI purpose code, and a CPA capital verification report. Keep all current account software service revenue separately documented with contracts, invoices, and service trade declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unattended remote screen-share and IoT telemetry data flows create data residency and data export risk; AML screening may flag encrypted remote-access software as a potential tool for unauthorized intrusion or cyber attack.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide product security whitepaper, penetration test report, end-user license agreement, privacy policy, data processing agreement, and cybersecurity registration or filing where applicable. Include an AML questionnaire clarifying that the remote access platform is used only for legitimate device support with authenticated endpoints, user consent, and no illegal intrusion or data exfiltration functionality.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The WFOE has no mandatory minimum capital requirement and may appear thin-capitalized; frequent intercompany payments to the Taiwan parent for management fees or technical royalties could be flagged as profit stripping, round-tripping, or transfer mispricing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a business plan with a capital benchmark based on projected 12-month operating burn; transfer pricing documentation covering related-party service fees; tax payment and withholding certificates; and detailed intercompany agreements with commercial substance, documented deliverables, and benchmarked arm's-length pricing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan shareholder should remit through its corporate account, never a personal account, to the WFOE's Foreign Exchange Capital Account at a SAFE-designated bank using SWIFT MT103. The remittance instruction must reference the FDI SAFE registration number and the correct balance-of-payments purpose code for equity capital injection. Upon receipt, the bank verifies the FX registration and underlying investment documents; a PRC CPA then issues a capital verification report. The funds cannot be settled into RMB before bank verification, and the capital account foreign exchange settlement form must be completed. Use of funds must align with the WFOE's registered business scope and the negative list. Inbound proceeds from Stripe or Paddle must not enter through the capital account; these are current account software subscription receipts and must be collected through a normal settlement account with service trade declarations and tax filings.

stage_4.outbound_trade_disbursements: For software maintenance, licensing, and support payments to foreign vendors, use SWIFT MT103 with supporting service trade contract, invoice, and tax certificate. For physical IoT hardware component procurement, use commercial letters of credit or documentary collections where bank trade finance guarantees are required. For cross-border RMB transactions, route through the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) with proper trade declarations. All outbound payments must pass through the bank's AML screening and SAFE current account declaration process; no offshore netting or treasury pooling should be attempted without SAFE approval.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/FX forward contracts and options with SAFE-designated domestic banks, permitted only with genuine current or capital account underlying exposure and no speculative or naked positions.

Cross-currency swaps between RMB and USD or other fully accessible major currencies to match long-term FDI capital injection, loan principal and interest, and profit repatriation cash flows, provided SAFE registration and real-demand documentation are maintained.

Onshore NDF-style structures are not permissible for the mainland WFOE; only the offshore parent may consider offshore RMB NDF markets, but such instruments cannot be intermediated through the mainland treasury or settled via an onshore Chinese bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Information Publicity Report (企业年度报告公示) — audited financial indicators, shareholder contribution status, and corporate change particulars for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually 1 January – 30 June for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late filing results in placement on the Operating Abnormal List (经营异常名录) and a public credit warning; unresolved for 3 consecutive years triggers inclusion in the Serious Illegal and Dishonest Enterprise List, joint-market sanctions, restriction of banking and credit facilities, and ultimate administrative revocation of the business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Settlement (企业所得税汇算清缴) — final CIT return, self-assessment, and settlement of payments for the preceding tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) — competent local tax authority of business registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May of the following tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of RMB 2,000–10,000; underpaid tax incurs a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the outstanding amount; understatement or concealment incurs a penalty of 50%–500% of the underpaid tax; deliberate evasion triggers criminal liability under PRC Criminal Law Article 201.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Information Annual Report (外商投资信息年度报告) — Taiwan investor identity, full foreign ownership chain, ultimate beneficial controller, and business status disclosure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) via the Foreign Investment Information Reporting System (jointly submitted through the SAMR annual report portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually 1 January – 30 June for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Warning and rectification order for non-reporting or false reporting; failure to rectify within the stipulated period exposes the WFOE to a fine of RMB 100,000–300,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Financial Report and CPA Audit Opinion (年度财务会计报告及审计报告) — audited statements prepared under ASBE by a PRC-licensed certified public accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Retained at the registered office; submitted with the CIT annual settlement package; available to SAMR, MOFCOM, and tax authorities on demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit completion required before the 31 May CIT settlement and 30 June SAMR annual report deadlines; prudent completion by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct filing penalty; however, absence of an audited report delays the CIT settlement and SAMR/MOFCOM annual reports, exposes the company to annual-filing-system penalties, blocks dividend remittance and equity or capital reduction procedures, and may trigger Company Law penalties for concealment or misrepresentation in financial disclosure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: PRC Company Law requires every company to prepare annual financial accounting reports and have them audited by a PRC-licensed CPA firm; no turnover, asset, or headcount threshold exempts a WFOE from this obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE), substantially convergent with IFRS; eligible small-and-medium companies may elect the ASBE for Small Enterprises (小企业会计准则); tax accounting adjustments follow the PRC Corporate Income Tax Law and its Implementing Regulations; accounting vouchers and ledgers are retained for 30 years and annual financial reports permanently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must confirm the ultimate Taiwan shareholder (实际控制人) and complete ownership chain in the SAMR annual information report and the MOFCOM foreign investment annual report. Any equity transfer requires a shareholders resolution, prompt update of the Register of Shareholders (股东名册), amendment of the Articles of Association, and SAMR re-registration within 30 days of transfer; updated UBO data flows into the next annual report cycle. The Taiwan parent is separately subject to the Taiwan Investment Commission's annual reporting obligations for mainland China investments.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors, Supervisors, and Senior Management (董事、监事和高级管理人员名册)
Share Transfer and Pledge Register (股权变更及出质登记记录)
Minutes of Shareholders' General Meetings (股东会会议记录)
Minutes of Board Meetings (董事会会议记录)
Financial Accounting Records and Annual Financial Reports (财务会计报告)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500–2,200 per year for registered physical address and licensed agency services in tier-1/2 PRC cities
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500–4,500 per year for a small-to-medium WFOE; USD 5,000–12,000 where group consolidation or transfer-pricing documentation is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% (Income Tax Act Article 5(5); effective from 2018 and currently in force)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% exempt on taxable income ≤ NT$120,000; 50% of excess for taxable income NT$120,001–NT$200,000; 20% on income > NT$200,000 (same 20% marginal rate with preferential effective rate for small bands). Additional incentives: 15% R&D tax credit up to NT$10 million per annum under Statute for Industrial Innovation Article 10; 5% retained-earnings surcharge applies to surplus not distributed by following year.
